itinerary.text: Report at 5:30 AM at Quaid-e-Azam University; the van leaves at 6:00 sharp, collecting from Kashmir Chowk, Abpara, G-8, H-9, G-13 and 26 Number. Up the Hazara Motorway with breakfast on the way, into Naran by 1 PM, then jeeps to Saif ul Malook Lake. Back in Naran for rafting and the zipline, hotel check-in at 6, and the evening in Naran Bazaar.

Wake-up call at 5, breakfast at Batakundi, then Lulusar Lake and up to Babusar Top by 10:30 — an hour at the pass, where snow is expected. Down through Kaghan Valley in the afternoon, dinner at Balakot, and back in Islamabad by around 11 PM.

steps.p: Say which trip and how many seats. Wahid answers it himself, usually the same day.
A seat is yours once the advance is in — trips are small and September fills early.
Pickup points and the packing list go out there a few days before.
The driving happens while you sleep. You wake up in the mountains.

faqs.q: Where does the van leave from?
faqs.a: Islamabad, always, and usually around midnight so the driving happens while you sleep. Pickup points go out in the WhatsApp group a few days before. Drop-off is back at the same points.
The van both ways, your bed, the meals listed on the trip page, and the local jeeps where the road needs them. It does not cover what you buy on the way, gear hire, or meals we have not listed.

faqs.q: Do I have to be a student?
faqs.a: No. The dates are planned around semesters and the prices around student budgets, but the van is open to anyone who travels well in a group.

faqs.q: How do I hold a seat?
faqs.a: Message the number. A seat is yours once the advance is in — trips are small and September fills early.

faqs.q: Can I come on my own, or bring family?
faqs.a: Both happen on most trips. Rooms are allocated separately for women travelling alone or in groups.

faqs.q: How high do we actually go, and does that matter?
faqs.a: Arang Kel tops out at 2,743 m, which nobody feels. The climb up from Kel is the part your legs notice, not your lungs — an hour or so on foot once the chairlift has taken you over the river.

A warm layer — it drops close to freezing up there at night in late September — shoes you can walk a rough track in, a power bank, your ID card, and any medicine you take. A full list goes out in the group before we leave.

reviews.text: Everything was sorted before we reached the pickup point. First time north and I never once felt lost.
The price on the poster was the price we paid. That alone is rare here.
Small van, good food, and someone who knew exactly when to leave to beat the traffic.

about.text: Northern Pakistan, planned and managed for you
Travel With Wahid plans and manages trips from Islamabad to northern Pakistan — fixed departures, custom group trips, and online booking with live seat availability.
Travel With Wahid runs trips from Islamabad to the valleys of northern Pakistan — the Neelum valley and Arang Kel, Swat and Kalam, Fairy Meadows, Kumrat, Naran and the Kalash valleys.
We manage the whole trip: the route and timings, transport, stays and the day-by-day plan, with support on the road from pickup to drop-off. All you have to do is turn up.
Booking takes a few minutes online. See how many seats are left on a departure in real time, get a booking reference straight away, and check your booking status any time with your email.
Travelling as a university society, a batch, a family or a group of friends? We build custom trips around your dates, your group and your budget.
